editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries (24, 29, 31) would mislead a learner. They keep the meaning, stay consistent with the rest of the page on "Pass Manager", "Stufe" and "dynamische Entkopplung", and use "du" throughout. Entry 29 has two small wording slips. First, "ein ... Layout ... auf das angegebene Zielgerät „einbettet“" uses the wrong preposition, since in German you embed something "in" a thing, not "auf" it. Second, "Stufen mit Funktionen" for "stages that provide common functionality" comes right after "Stufengeneratorfunktionen", so a reader could take "Funktionen" to mean Python functions. "Funktionalität" avoids that.

editor_note: Entries 32 and 36 are accurate and read naturally. "Entartung" is the correct German term for degeneracy, and "im mittleren Block lokalisiert" matches the source. Entry 49 is accurate but has two small problems. It renders "any" as "jedem" twice ("auf jedem der neun Qubits", "ein $Z$-Fehler auf jedem Block"), which a reader can take as "each/every" rather than "any one". Its closing relative clause also makes the argument, not the ordering of the gates, what yields the equivalent circuits. Neither changes what a learner would take away in context, and the "Die Tatsache, dass … folgt daraus, dass …" construction is stiff and copies the English sentence structure.

All five rewritten entries (5, 6, 22, 62, 82) keep the source meaning: the linear-code closure property under ⊕, the parity-check definition, the independence of X and Z correction, and the caveat that different shifts u can give the same vector. Nothing here would mislead a learner. Two phrasings are stiff enough that a native editor would change them. editor_note: Entries 21 and 32 match the English. Entry 21 keeps "linear in $N$", "$N/2$ Versuche" and "wie $\sqrt{N}$ skaliert". Entry 32 keeps the source's own typo "$|+\rangle$ und $|+\rangle$", which should read $|+\rangle$ and $|-\rangle$. That typo should be fixed upstream, not in the translation. In entry 146, "stößt auch die $\sqrt{N}$-Verbesserung schnell an ihre Grenzen" adds "schnell" ("quickly"), which the English "only goes so far" does not say. The claim gets a little stronger, but a learner would not be misled. "in ein Quanten-Orakel kodiert" is also slightly stiff, and "in einem Quantenorakel kodiert" reads more naturally.

examples.line_approx: Und bei einem exponentiell wachsenden Suchraum ...
examples.source: And for an exponentially growing search space, even the $\sqrt{N}$ improvement only goes so far.
examples.translation: Und bei einem exponentiell wachsenden Suchraum stößt auch die $\sqrt{N}$-Verbesserung schnell an ihre Grenzen.
examples.suggested: Und bei einem exponentiell wachsenden Suchraum stößt auch die $\sqrt{N}$-Verbesserung an ihre Grenzen.
examples.why: 'schnell' adds a claim of speed that the source does not make. The strengthening is mild, so this is a minor issue and would not mislead a learner.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries would mislead a learner, and entry 10 ("wobei sich die meisten Notebooks auch unverändert ausführen lassen") reads natively. In entry 9, "$2 \times 2$-Matrizen reichen aus" drops the English hedge "should be sufficient" and turns it into a flat promise. "sollten ausreichen" would keep the hedge. In entry 5, "in deutlich weniger Zeit abgeschlossen werden als die kostenlose Zeit im Rahmen des Open Plans" is a stiff, literal comparison. A native editor would name the free-time quota explicitly as an "Zeitkontingent".

examples.source: Some linear algebra background ( $2 \times 2$ matrices should be sufficient)
examples.translation: Grundkenntnisse in linearer Algebra ($2 \times 2$-Matrizen reichen aus)
examples.suggested: Grundkenntnisse in linearer Algebra ($2 \times 2$-Matrizen sollten ausreichen)
examples.why: The hedge 'should be' is dropped, so a tentative estimate becomes a flat promise. Minor, and not misleading in practice.

examples.source: All activities can be completed in much less time than the free time allotted as part of the Open Plan available to all users.
examples.translation: Alle Aktivitäten können in deutlich weniger Zeit abgeschlossen werden als die kostenlose Zeit im Rahmen des Open Plans, der allen Benutzern zur Verfügung steht.
examples.suggested: Alle Aktivitäten benötigen deutlich weniger Zeit als das kostenlose Zeitkontingent des Open Plans, der allen Nutzenden zur Verfügung steht.
examples.why: This literal comparison ('in weniger Zeit ... als die kostenlose Zeit') is stiff. Naming the 'Zeitkontingent' reads more naturally.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entries 2 and 20 are accurate, and entry 20 correctly keeps the "may be re-applied" caveat ("können ... wieder angewendet werden"). Entry 29 has two small problems. First, "jede eindeutige Stichprobe" is a calque of "unique sample". "Eindeutig" means "unambiguous", but the source means "distinct", so "jede verschiedene/einzelne Stichprobe" is correct here. Second, the gloss "(d. h. des ungeschnittenen Circuits)" is not in the source. It is accurate, but a translator added it and it should be removed.

examples.source: one combined coefficient is given for each unique sample
examples.translation: für jede eindeutige Stichprobe wird ein kombinierter Koeffizient angegeben
examples.suggested: für jede unterschiedliche Stichprobe wird ein kombinierter Koeffizient angegeben
examples.why: This is a calque. 'Eindeutig' means 'unambiguous', not 'distinct/unique', so the phrase reads oddly, though it does not mislead in this context.

examples.source: To simulate the expectation value of the full-sized circuit

examples.suggested: Um den Erwartungswert des Circuits in voller Größe zu simulieren

editor_note: Neither rewritten entry would mislead a learner. Entry 0 and most of the table in entry 6 are faithful and read naturally (for example "Operator-Rückwärtspropagierung zur Reduzierung der Circuit-Tiefe" and "Sample-basierte Quantendiagonalisierung zur Schätzung des Grundzustands"). The one slip is in the AQC-Tensor row: "Approximierte Quantenkompilierung" means "approximated compilation". The usual German adjective for "approximate" is "approximative", so a native editor would write "Approximative Quantenkompilierung".

examples.source: Approximate Quantum Compilation with tensor networks
examples.translation: Approximierte Quantenkompilierung mit Tensornetzwerken
examples.suggested: Approximative Quantenkompilierung mit Tensornetzwerken
examples.why: 'approximiert' is a past participle ('approximated'). The method name calls for the adjective 'approximativ', which is the idiomatic German term for an approximate method.

editor_note: None of the 8 rewritten entries changes the meaning. Conditions, quantities and caveats all match the English, including the lightcone exclusion in [4], the backward-to-forward switch point in [82], and the zero-bias versus tunable-bias trade-off in [108]. The remaining problems are wording. In [100], "Mit den begrenzten Fehlern" and "starken Rechenressourcen" are calques ("mit den Fehlerschranken", "leistungsstarken" would be natural). In [108], "Sampling-Budget" sits next to "Stichprobenaufwand" in the same paragraph, "Benutzer" is used where the rest of the page has "Nutzer", and "wenn man anfänglich einen Workflow prototypisiert" is stiff. The parenthetical in [35], "nämlich sollten wir…", has the word order of an English calque.

examples.source: With the bounded errors from our quantum circuit ... by utilizing the strong compute resources from our cluster

examples.suggested: Mit den Fehlerschranken für unseren Circuit ... durch die Nutzung der leistungsstarken Rechenressourcen unseres Clusters
examples.why: "begrenzte Fehler" reads as "small errors" rather than "errors for which we computed bounds", and "starke Rechenressourcen" is a calque.

examples.source: This helps let the user stay within a fixed sampling budget, which can be particularly useful when initially prototyping a workflow.
examples.translation: Dies ermöglicht es dem Benutzer, innerhalb eines festen Sampling-Budgets zu bleiben, was besonders nützlich sein kann, wenn man anfänglich einen Workflow prototypisiert.
examples.suggested: So kannst du innerhalb eines festen Stichprobenbudgets bleiben, was besonders beim ersten Prototyping eines Workflows nützlich ist.
examples.why: "Sampling-Budget" clashes with "Stichprobenaufwand" earlier in the same paragraph, "Benutzer" clashes with "Nutzer" used elsewhere on the page, and "wenn man anfänglich ... prototypisiert" is stiff.

examples.source: (namely, we should measure an observable of 1)
examples.translation: (nämlich sollten wir einen Observable-Wert von 1 messen)
examples.suggested: (wir sollten nämlich einen Observablenwert von 1 messen)

editor_note: None of the 9 rewritten entries misleads a learner. The caveats about feedforward latency (entries 9, 43, 72), the odd-parity phase explanation (30), the conditional measure_2 support (63) and the "comparable durations" claim (82) all match the English. Two small polish items remain. Entry 30 writes "Dazu ist folgendes zu beachten", but the nominalized form is capitalized: "Folgendes". Entry 72 uses the mis-bracketed compound "der dynamische Circuit-Ansatz", while the rest of the page consistently says "Implementierung/Ansatz mit dynamischen Circuits".

examples.source: To understand this, note that the ZZ rotations apply a phase factor
examples.translation: Dazu ist folgendes zu beachten: ZZ-Rotationen wenden einen Phasenfaktor ...
examples.suggested: Dazu ist Folgendes zu beachten: ZZ-Rotationen wenden einen Phasenfaktor ...

examples.source: the dynamic circuit approach yields a significantly shorter two-qubit depth

examples.suggested: der Ansatz mit dynamischen Circuits eine deutlich kürzere Zwei-Qubit-Tiefe

editor_note: Entries 18, 34 and 49 say the same thing as the English and would not mislead a learner. The CDF explanation keeps its meaning: "höchstens diesen MSE", the steep and slow rise, and "am weitesten links liegende Punkte" are all correct. A native editor would still fix a few compound words: "Vier-Qubit-Initial-Layout" (entry 34) is a clumsy mix of German and English, "dynamische Schaltkreis-Funktionen" (entry 18) puts the adjective on the wrong noun, and "Bell-Zustand-Güte" (entry 49) is missing its linking s ("Bell-Zustands-Güte"). The translation of "mid-circuit measurement" also varies: entry 34 has "Messungen mitten im Ablauf", while entry 49 has "Messungen mitten im Schaltkreis".

examples.source: For each four-qubit initial layout
examples.translation: Für jedes Vier-Qubit-Initial-Layout
examples.suggested: Für jedes initiale Vier-Qubit-Layout
examples.why: The hyphenated compound mixes German and English awkwardly; a German technical writer would use the adjective form.

examples.source: dynamic circuit features
examples.translation: dynamische Schaltkreis-Funktionen
examples.suggested: Funktionen für dynamische Schaltkreise
examples.why: As written, 'dynamisch' describes 'Schaltkreis-Funktionen' instead of 'Schaltkreise', which is a calque of the English noun stack.

examples.translation: die Bell-Zustand-Güte
examples.suggested: die Bell-Zustands-Güte
examples.why: The compound is missing its linking s (Fugen-s).

examples.translation: Messungen mitten im Ablauf
examples.suggested: Messungen mitten im Schaltkreis
examples.why: Entry 49 translates the same term as 'Messungen mitten im Schaltkreis'. It should be one term within the file.

editor_note: All seven rewritten titles say what their English sources say, and their terms match the rest of the page: 'Gepoolte sample-basierte Quantendiagonalisierung eines Kern-Hamiltonians' follows [16], 'maximale unabhängige Menge' is the standard German term, and 'Market-Split-Problem' is written the same way as in [67].

The meaning holds throughout, including the parts that are easy to get wrong: the upper-bound and monotonicity claims, the sign-versus-support argument for qubit excitations, and the M_J product-stage reasoning. I found no semantic drift. What is left is surface polish. There are grammar slips: "um zu *vorschlagen*" in [22], the neuter "ein nukleares Schalenmodell-Hamiltonian" in [9], and "eine … abgelesene Kosten" in [78]. In [165], "core energy" becomes "Kernenergie", which reads as "nuclear energy"; the file uses "Kernrumpf" for "core" everywhere else. Several terms are also rendered inconsistently: support is "Träger" in [72] but "Support" in [144]/[145]/[174]; the method is both "Pooled SQD" and "gepooltes SQD"; run is both "Lauf" and "Durchlauf"; and the link text "[Background]" stays in English in [104] while "Hintergrund" is used in [92].

examples.source: A quantum circuit is used only to *propose* which basis states matter.
examples.translation: Ein Quanten-Circuit wird nur verwendet, um zu *vorschlagen*, welche Basiszustände relevant sind.
examples.suggested: Ein Quanten-Circuit dient nur dazu, *vorzuschlagen*, welche Basiszustände relevant sind.
examples.why: Ungrammatical infinitive: with a separable verb the German form is "vorzuschlagen", not "zu vorschlagen".

examples.source: where an oscillator frequency and a core energy would plausibly go
examples.translation: wo plausibel eine Oszillatorfrequenz und eine Kernenergie stehen würden
examples.suggested: wo plausibel eine Oszillatorfrequenz und eine Rumpfenergie (Kernrumpfenergie) stehen würden
examples.why: "Kernenergie" normally means nuclear energy. The rest of the file uses "Kernrumpf" for the inert core.

examples.source: Learn how a nuclear shell-model Hamiltonian ... becomes a qubit Hamiltonian
examples.translation: Lerne, wie ein nukleares Schalenmodell-Hamiltonian ... zu einem Qubit-Hamiltonian ... wird
examples.suggested: Lerne, wie ein nuklearer Schalenmodell-Hamiltonian ... zu einem Qubit-Hamiltonian ... wird
examples.why: Wrong gender: "Hamiltonian" is masculine everywhere else in the file.

examples.source: only its support to be useful
examples.translation: nur einen nützlichen Support
examples.suggested: nur einen nützlichen Träger
examples.why: [72] renders support as "Träger" (the correct mathematical term), while [144], [145] and [174] use the anglicism "Support".

examples.source: because a cost read off an abstract circuit is not the cost the transpiler produces
examples.translation: weil eine an einem abstrakten Circuit abgelesene Kosten nicht die Kosten sind
examples.suggested: weil die an einem abstrakten Circuit abgelesenen Kosten nicht die Kosten sind, die der Transpiler erzeugt
examples.why: "Kosten" is plural in German, so the singular article "eine" is ungrammatical.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout: the x_j=1 to Region A and x_j=0 to Region B assignment, the d_i/2 target and the option semantics in [47] all match the English, and the du-register holds. A native editor would still change a few things. "Binary assignment vector" is "Zuweisungsvektor" in [17] but "Zuordnungsvektor" in [53]. "Demand" is "Nachfrage" everywhere except "Unternehmensbedarfs" in [53]. "Feasibility constraint" is calqued as "Machbarkeitsbedingung", where German optimization usage is "Zulässigkeitsbedingung". "traditionellen erschöpfenden Suchen" and "Lagerüberläufe" read as translationese.

examples.source: The optimization or feasibility constraint requires
examples.translation: Die Optimierungs- bzw. Machbarkeitsbedingung verlangt
examples.suggested: Die Optimierungs- bzw. Zulässigkeitsbedingung verlangt
examples.why: In German optimization terminology, 'feasibility' is 'Zulässigkeit' (zulässige Lösung). 'Machbarkeit' is a calque.

examples.source: represents a binary assignment vector ... half of the total company demand
examples.translation: einen binären Zuordnungsvektor ... die Hälfte des gesamten Unternehmensbedarfs
examples.suggested: einen binären Zuweisungsvektor ... die Hälfte der gesamten Nachfrage des Unternehmens
examples.why: Entry [17] uses 'Zuweisungsvektor' and the rest of the file uses 'Nachfrage' for demand. Switching terms here is inconsistent.

examples.source: using traditional exhaustive searches
examples.translation: mit traditionellen erschöpfenden Suchen
examples.suggested: mit klassischer vollständiger Suche (Brute Force)
examples.why: The plural calque 'erschöpfende Suchen' is stiff. 'vollständige Suche' or 'Brute-Force-Suche' is the idiomatic term.

examples.source: localized product shortages or warehouse overflows
examples.translation: lokalisierte Produktengpässe oder Lagerüberläufe
examples.suggested: lokale Produktengpässe oder überfüllte Lager
examples.why: 'Lagerüberläufe' is a literal calque, and 'lokalisierte' is anglicized. Neither reads naturally in German.

examples.source: saved your account to your local environment
examples.translation: dass du dein Konto bereits gespeichert hast
examples.suggested: dass du dein Konto bereits in deiner lokalen Umgebung gespeichert hast
examples.why: This drops the qualifier 'to your local environment'. It is minor, but it tells the learner where the credentials are expected to be.

editor_note: The rewritten heading [24] "Graph -> Hamiltonoperator" is accurate and uses the standard German term, so it does not mislead a learner. The problem is that the rewrite leaves the file inconsistent. The paragraph right under this heading, [29], still says "den Graphen mithilfe von PCE in einen Hamiltonian kodieren", so the heading uses one term and the text below it uses another. Keep [24] as it is and change [29] to "in einen Hamiltonoperator kodieren".

examples.source: Graph -> Hamiltonian
examples.translation: Graph -> Hamiltonoperator
examples.suggested: Keep [24]; align [29] to "...mithilfe von PCE in einen Hamiltonoperator kodieren."
examples.why: The rendering is correct, but the paragraph under this heading ([29]) uses the anglicism "Hamiltonian" for the same concept. This mismatch within the file is minor and does not mislead.

editor_note: The rewritten heading in entry 53, "Stützvektormaschine (SVM)", is accurate: it names the same classifier and does not mislead. The problem is that it breaks consistency with entry 11, which calls the same concept "Support-Vektor-Maschinen". German ML writing more often keeps the English "Support Vector Machine", so it would be better to bring the heading in line with entry 11's form (or the plain English term) than to add a second rendering. Because the "(SVM)" abbreviation stays in both places, the concept is still easy to recognize, which makes this a minor issue.

examples.source: Support Vector Machine (SVM) {#support-vector-machine-svm}
examples.translation: Stützvektormaschine (SVM) {#support-vector-machine-svm}
examples.suggested: Support-Vektor-Maschine (SVM) {#support-vector-machine-svm}
examples.why: The term is correct, but entry 11 renders the same concept as "Support-Vektor-Maschinen", so the file now uses two terms for one idea. The Anglicized form is also the more common one in German ML texts. Aligning the heading with entry 11 keeps the terminology consistent.

editor_note: None of the six rewritten entries would mislead a learner. OBP's trade-off (a shallower circuit in exchange for more operator measurements), 'unbiased' as 'unverzerrt' and the claim about classical hardness all keep their meaning. Two wording problems remain. First, 'tilted-field' is rendered as the invented compound 'Kippfeld' ('2D-Kippfeld-Ising(-Modell)') in entries 1, 7 and 12; German physics usage is 'Ising-Modell im gekippten/geneigten Feld'. Second, entry 52 copies the English literally: 'zwei Schichten des Circuits reduziert hat' should say that the circuit lost two layers ('um zwei Schichten verkürzt').

examples.source: Simulate 2D tilted-field Ising with the QESEM function
examples.translation: 2D-Kippfeld-Ising mit der QESEM-Funktion simulieren
examples.suggested: 2D-Ising-Modell im gekippten Feld mit der QESEM-Funktion simulieren
examples.why: 'Kippfeld' is not an established German physics term. The usual phrasing is 'Ising-Modell im gekippten/geneigten Feld'. The same coinage appears again in entries 7 and 12.

examples.source: We can see that the backpropagation reduced two layers of the circuit.
examples.translation: Wir sehen, dass die Rückwärtspropagation zwei Schichten des Circuits reduziert hat.
examples.suggested: Wir sehen, dass die Rückwärtspropagation den Circuit um zwei Schichten verkürzt hat.
examples.why: Literal copy of the English: 'Schichten reduzieren' suggests the layers were shrunk, not removed. The intended meaning is that two layers were removed, so the circuit got shallower.

editor_note: Entry 7 is faithful overall and uses "du" correctly. It drops the qualifier "random-bond", though: "zufälligen 156-Qubit-Ising-Modells" says only that the model is random, not that its couplings are random. That matters because the spin-glass framing in [22] depends on the random couplings. It is a flattened qualifier rather than a misleading claim. Also, "binäre Optimierungsziele" is a slightly loose rendering of "binary optimization objectives", since the rest of the page consistently uses "Zielfunktion" for "objective function".

examples.source: the ground-state energy of a random-bond 156-qubit Ising model possessing cubic terms
examples.translation: die Grundzustandsenergie eines zufälligen 156-Qubit-Ising-Modells mit kubischen Termen
examples.suggested: die Grundzustandsenergie eines 156-Qubit-Ising-Modells mit zufälligen Kopplungen (Random-Bond) und kubischen Termen
examples.why: The translation drops 'random-bond', which says the couplings are random. 'zufälliges Ising-Modell' is vaguer, although not false.

examples.source: problems formulated as supported binary optimization objectives
examples.translation: Probleme ..., die als unterstützte binäre Optimierungsziele formuliert sind
examples.suggested: Probleme ..., die sich als unterstützte binäre Zielfunktionen formulieren lassen
examples.why: The rest of the file uses 'Zielfunktion' for 'objective function' ([10], [21], [22], [28]). 'Optimierungsziele' is defensible but does not match.

editor_note: All four rewritten entries (8, 15, 148, 179) are faithful and read naturally: "Zielumsatz", "ausmultiplizieren", "Standardwert `2` führt im Allgemeinen zum kleinsten Circuit" and "klassische Solver an ihre Grenzen stoßen" keep the source's quantities, hedges and claims, and the Circuit/Schaltkreistiefe mix in 148 is left to the leak sweep.

All four rewritten entries (8, 10, 11, 30) keep the English meaning, with no drift, hallucination or dropped caveats: the mixed-state caveat and the "tomographisch vollständiger Basissatz wie die Pauli-Basis" aside survive in [11], the claim "nach $\frac{n}{2}$ Qubits korrekt eingefügt" is intact in [30], and "Circuit Knitting"/"Subcircuits"/"Sampler-Primitives" are used consistently with the rest of the page.

All five rewritten entries keep their meaning: the CNOT condition in [32] ("nur dann …, wenn das erste Qubit |1⟩ ist, andernfalls bleibt das zweite Qubit unverändert") is intact, the reordered Hadamard sentence in [27] still says superposition means equal chances of 1 and 0, and "Ansätze und Circuit-Bibliothek" [141] matches the term used in [142].

Both rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally: in [40] "mit T1-Zeiten von ~50–100 µs" and "Transpiliere die Circuits für dieses Backend" keep the numbers and the steps from the English, and [59] keeps the 2 % symmetric readout error ("eine 0 wird als 1 gelesen oder eine 1 als 0"), using du and "Mess-Circuit" in line with the rest of the file.
